title: A HOME THAT MATCHES THE MESSAGE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'The woman he marries must be a virgin. He must not marry a widow, a
divorced woman, or a woman defiled by prostitution, but only a virgin
from his own people, so that he will not defile his offspring among
his people. I am the LORD, who makes him holy'" - Lev 21:13-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Again the standard for the high priest is stricter than for others.
Note carefully what this is not saying. It is not saying widows or
divorced women are second-class before God. Scripture is full of God's
special care for widows (Ps 68:5; Jas 1:27). Ruth was a widow and
became the great-grandmother of King David.

This was a specific requirement for one office, to keep the family
line of Israel's chief representative visibly and unquestionably
undivided. In a culture where symbols carried enormous weight, the high
priest's household had to be beyond public dispute.

And once more the chapter ends the thought the same way: "I am the
LORD, who makes him holy." Even the high priest did not make himself
holy. God did.

Dear friend, this is the thread running through the whole chapter. Every
rule points to a God who is set apart and who graciously sets apart
His people.

Christ, our High Priest, has a bride too - the church. And Paul says
He gave Himself up for her to make her holy, cleansing her, to present
her to Himself radiant and blameless (Eph 5:25-27). The church was not
already spotless. He made her so.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does it change me to know Christ is making His church radiant?
2. Am I treating any group of people as second-class in God's family?
3. Where do I need to stop striving and receive the holiness God gives?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, thank You for loving Your church and making her clean. Do
that work in me, and help me honour every person You have welcomed.
Amen.
